summary: Gives good vs bad patterns for prefixing or suffixing each list item with map('regex_replace'), notes the pre-2.0 backslash escaping rule, and shows regex_escape for Python and POSIX basic regexes.
questions: How do I add https:// to every item in a list?
How do I append :80 to each host in a list?
How do I escape special characters for use in a regex?
Do I need four backslashes for backreferences in YAML?

answer_card.title: Prefixing list items and escaping regexes
answer_card.answer_md:
```jinja
{{ hosts | map('regex_replace', '^(.*)$', 'https://\\1') | list }}   # good
{{ hosts | map('regex_replace', '^', 'https://') | list }}           # good
{{ hosts | map('regex_replace', '$', ':80') | list }}                # good
{{ hosts | map('regex_replace', '(.*)', 'https://\\1') | list }}     # bad
```

Escape a regex:

```jinja
{{ '^f.*o(.*)$' | regex_escape() }}               # Python
{{ '^f.*o(.*)$' | regex_escape('posix_basic') }}  # 2.8+
```

The four-backslash rule for backreferences only applied before Ansible 2.0.
